clue.text: Plentiful supply coming from British sailor and German worker

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is the usual crossword rating for a British sailor
und is the German word for 'and'
the ant is the crossword's standard worker insect

explanation.surface: A bountiful supply provided by a seaman from Britain and a labourer from Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and German' is one piece: the German word for 'and', UND. 'supply coming from' just links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something existing in large, generous quantity; they are synonyms.

clue.text: On a winding road it is showing skill

indicators.note: a winding road twists about, so the letters of road and it are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Negotiating a twisty road demonstrates a driver's ability.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winding' rearranges ROAD plus IT; 'On a' and 'is' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone deft and dexterous is displaying skill; the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Neat and dry

explanation.surface: A description of a spirit drunk without a mixer.
explanation.walkthrough: Neat spirit has had no water added; dry ground has had no water given to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat whisky has no water added, and parched land that is dry has received no irrigation: both lack added water.

clue.text: Turn nasty in play

parts.note: a nasty situation is a dangerous one
a turn in the road is a corner

explanation.surface: A character in a drama turns unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: The play is by J.B. Priestley (1932). The pieces are placed in answer order: 'nasty' gives the first word, 'Turn' the second.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the title of a stage drama by the English writer J.B. Priestley.

clue.text: Dashed up with class report

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written from the bottom upwards, so it reads backwards

parts.note: dashed means ran, as in hurried
a class or grade is a rate, as in first-rate

explanation.surface: Someone hurried upstairs with a school report.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RAN into NAR, which is followed by RATE; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To report events is to recount or tell them; synonyms.

clue.text: Teacher's ambition is to impose capital punishment

explanation.surface: A teacher secretly longs to execute pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as BE HEAD, it is what an ambitious teacher wants: to become head teacher. As one word it means to execute by decapitation.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacher hopes for promotion to head of the school; and decapitation is a form of execution.

clue.text: Prompt payment may be what archaeologists are looking for

explanation.surface: Paying a bill quickly is compared to an archaeological dig.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying a debt before it falls due is settling early; archaeologists dig for ancient villages and dwellings from long ago.

clue.text: Irene ruined him

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked or spoilt, so the name Irene is broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Irene was the downfall of some man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'him' is the definition: a man's name, matching the woman's name being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A male first name, so a fair stand-in for an unnamed man.

clue.text: Dicky disowned, fades away

indicators.note: dicky is British slang for weak or faulty, so the letters of disowned are taken as unsound and rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Dicky, cut off by his family, slowly withdraws from view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a name, but it is the British word for shaky or unreliable, signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A noise or wind that subsides gradually is diminishing; synonyms.

clue.text: Act wrongly and pinch a plant

indicators.note: wrongly means in an incorrect way, so the letters of act are put in the wrong order

parts.note: to pinch is to nip

explanation.surface: Misbehave and steal a houseplant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' turns ACT into CAT; then NIP. 'pinch' suggests stealing but here means squeeze.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a herb of the mint family that attracts cats.

clue.text: A worn out tree

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of a worn are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tree that is worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: The mountain ash, a tree with red berries.

clue.text: Make changes behind cook's fireplace

parts.note: behind means rear, the back part
a range is a kitchen stove, a cook's fire

explanation.surface: Alterations at the back of a kitchen hearth.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter the order or layout of things is to make changes.

clue.text: Where the seas are high, generally

explanation.surface: A sea-going description of a general state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' is an old word for the open ocean, so on it is out on the high seas; as a phrase it also means for the most part.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a literary name for the open ocean; the idiom also means on the whole, mostly.

clue.text: Agree to show an interest in investment

explanation.surface: Consent to display a share in a financial stake.
explanation.definitionFit: To give way or concede is to agree; and the return or income on an investment is what it produces.

clue.text: Go over undulating track

indicators.note: undulating means rising and falling in waves, so the letters of go over are rearranged

explanation.surface: Walk again across a hilly path.
explanation.definitionFit: A groove is a channel or rut, as in a record's track.

clue.text: A show presented before the show

definitions.text: A show presented before the show

parts.words: A show presented before the show
parts.note: a showing that comes before a production's official opening for critics or the public

explanation.surface: An opening act comes before the main performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A screening or performance given in advance of the public opening.

clue.text: Even the most generous would be deaf to such appeals

definitions.text: Even the most generous would be deaf to such appeals

parts.words: Even the most generous would be deaf to such appeals
parts.note: requests for charity that nobody responds to, because no one can hear them at all

explanation.surface: Some pleas for help fail to move even the kindest people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deaf to' suggests unmoved, but it is literal: the appeals are too quiet to be heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Appeals too quiet to be heard cannot be answered by anyone.

clue.text: Apt to be not on the level

explanation.surface: Someone liable to be dishonest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not on the level' suggests dishonest, but it means sloping.
explanation.definitionFit: Being disposed or likely to do something is being apt; and a sloping surface is tilted, not level.

clue.text: They don't like to assume anything

definitions.text: They don't like to assume anything

parts.words: They don't like to assume anything
parts.note: assume is read as put on clothing: these people prefer to wear nothing at all

explanation.surface: Careful people who never take anything for granted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assume' means presume in the surface but means put on, as clothes, in the solution.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturists prefer to go unclothed, not putting any garment on.

clue.text: Changes of clothing

explanation.surface: Swapping one outfit for another.
explanation.definitionFit: Shifts are alterations or moves; and a shift is also a loose straight dress, an item of clothing.

clue.text: Its contents are still to be dealt with

definitions.text: Its contents are still to be dealt with

parts.words: Its contents are still to be dealt with
parts.note: an office tray of papers awaiting attention, the desk's unanswered pile

explanation.surface: An unfinished job list waiting on someone's desk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dealt with' might suggest cards; it means handled in an office.
explanation.definitionFit: The desk receptacle that holds letters and papers awaiting attention.

clue.text: Swarms over nests if disturbed

indicators.note: disturbed means stirred up, so the letters of nests if are thrown about and rearranged

explanation.surface: Insects swarm over their nests when disturbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Pests that overrun a place in large numbers are swarming over it.

clue.text: Casually raise the volume?

parts.note: turning the pages of a book in a leisurely way, with volume read as a book rather than loudness

explanation.surface: Turning up the sound without much thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'volume' suggests loudness but means a book: to pick one up and leaf through it idly.
explanation.definitionFit: To look through a book casually, skimming its pages, is the idea.

clue.text: Catch a girl with nothing on

indicators.note: on means placed next to, so the zero is attached after the girl

parts.note: a lass is a girl
nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Nab a naked young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with nothing on' suggests nakedness; it puts O after LASS.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope with a noose is used to catch cattle; the word is also the verb for snaring them so.

clue.text: Name of doctor caught in malpractice

indicators.note: caught in means held inside, so the doctor is placed within the wrongdoing

parts.note: malpractice is wrongdoing, a sin
MO is Medical Officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor's name is identified in a negligence case.
explanation.walkthrough: MO goes inside SIN, giving SI-MO-N.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a man's first name.

clue.text: Silly man

parts.note: silly is a cricket term for fielding positions close to the batsman, so this is a player placed there

explanation.surface: A foolish fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, silly point and silly mid-off are close fielding positions; the fielder there is not foolish but brave.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket fielder near the bat stands in the field, close in, as at silly point.

clue.text: Proposes someone from Minnesota

indicators.note: from here means made out of, so the answer is built from the letters of Minnesota

explanation.surface: Someone from Minnesota puts forward a candidate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'someone' is a link to the wordplay; 'from' tells you the answer is made out of MINNESOTA's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone forward as a candidate is to propose them.

clue.text: Drinking bender

parts.note: a bender is a joint that bends, and this one bends to lift a glass when drinking

explanation.surface: A heavy drinking session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bender' suggests a drinking spree; it is the arm joint. 'Bending the' joint is British slang for drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: The arm joint flexes to raise a glass, hence the phrase bending it for heavy drinking.

clue.text: They've taken food off plates and rinsed out

indicators.note: out means disordered, so the letters of rinsed are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Once dinner is eaten, the dishes are rinsed out.
explanation.definitionFit: People eating at a restaurant clear their plates by eating the food.

clue.text: So to speak, ungrammatically, like it used to be

definitions.text: ungrammatically, like it used to be

explanation.surface: A comment on careless grammar.
explanation.walkthrough: Correct grammar would say 'as it was'; the subjunctive form used for 'like it used to be' is the ungrammatical reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means in a manner of speaking; read literally it is 'in the way it was', with the subjunctive wrongly used.
